images.title: Hunting Approach
images.scene: A field-manual study of observation, screened approach and a clear return route.
images.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Wide 16:9 mid-century field manual plate in fine NAVY ink and muted sage, dusty blue, ochre and coral pastel watercolor washes on ivory paper. Reference original digging-stick plate for STYLE ONLY. Title 'HUNTING APPROACH'. One small generic clothed field observer kneels at the sheltered near side of a rocky shoulder in image LEFT, watching TWO small red-deer hinds across an open patch to image RIGHT. He is an educational figure, not the traveller; plain shirt and trousers allowed. No modern weapon, rifle, bow, scope or binoculars. Main diagram shows cover, a shallow stony dip obstructing a direct closer route, and a clearly marked short RETURN route behind observer away from animals. Sparse arrows, no numeric distance or guaranteed cast. THREE short labels only: 'OBSERVE', 'REASSESS', 'KEEP A RETURN ROUTE'. One small inset of grass leaning with local breeze arrow, no compass or exact scent plume. Animals have ordinary anatomy, no antlers on females, no impact or injury. Plenty of space and legible simplified terrain. This is a judgement principle diagram, NOT a surveyed valley map, killing recipe or guarantee of approach range.
images.review: Accepted: checked anatomy, modest clothing, object construction and dated scene state.

images.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Wide 16:9 watercolor and fine brown ink on textured paper, original reference ONLY for protagonist identity and art style. New independent scene: medium close THREE-QUARTER FRONT view during a dry gathering walk AWAY from camp in open rocky northern Iberian oak/hazel woodland, autumn around 40,000 BP. NO SHELTER, HEARTH, RIVER OR BUILDINGS visible; crop from above head to below knees so garment details have clear space. Lean ordinary adult male with short tousled dark brown hair, short beard, natural skin without tattoos or body marks. Bark waist panels and small pelvic pad. No boots or trousers. He wears a NEW FLEXIBLE GOLDEN GRASS FRONT PANEL from below collarbones to waist, roughly 0.45 m across by 0.6 m long. It consists of many soft hanging grass bundles retained by exactly TWO distinct horizontal paired-yarn twining ROWS: ONE row at upper quarter, ANOTHER separate row near middle. These TWO rows are well separated and BOTH clearly visible across the full front panel, in addition to a separate thick flexible cord HEADER at the top. The top is a wrapped cord/grass bundle, NOT a wooden rod. Lower grass fringe hangs freely, no rigid willow basket weave or woven cloth. Original separate back panel of same flexible grass family is partly visible beyond side gap, not a full shirt; arms and sides free. Narrow fox-skin strip lies on anatomical LEFT shoulder (image RIGHT), hanging down BESIDE front grass panel, not a large fur cloak or collar. A NEW SMALL light gray-brown rabbit-fur CROWN PAD on TOP of head only, shallow folded shape with one narrow loose band around forehead/back of head, no chin tie. Ears, face, much nape exposed, short hair visible at forehead/sides, no giant hood or animal-face headdress. He stops and re-seats ONE accessible shoulder fastening with his right hand at image LEFT. Other hand relaxed low. Natural hands, exactly two arms and two legs. No spear needed. Quiet concentration, morning dry light, sparse autumn woodland rocks, no carcass, labels, fletched darts, modern kit or future clothes. Make BOTH separate front retaining rows unmistakable; preserve a modest primitive garment with remaining coverage gaps.
images.review: Accepted: both retaining rows and separate flexible header visible; crown pad has exposed ears/face, separate left fox strip, paired core panels with side gaps; no future objects or changed camp geometry in crop.

images.scene: Watching a distant wolf-like canid at the southwest dirty flank, with his spear ready and open ground between them.
images.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Wide watercolor and brown ink illustration for an early-prehistory handbook. Reference gives ONLY the man's identity and painting style. Autumn northern Iberia 40,000 BP, rocky open oak woodland, wet leaves after showers. The familiar lean short-dark-haired, short-bearded man stands upright in RIGHT foreground, barefoot, bark waist panels and small pelvic pad. Narrow fox-fur strip on his anatomical LEFT shoulder hanging down front. No grass garment worn, no hat, no new front covering. Exactly two arms, two legs. He holds a plain WOODEN-POINTED spear LOW with both hands, watching rather than fighting. A SINGLE normal adult grey-brown wolf-like canid is in LEFT middle distance, at the far edge of the southwest dirty-work area, quietly sniffing ground. Broad EMPTY ground clearly separates them. No snarling, leap, attack, injury or carcass. A small rough drying frame is visible near the distant brush, holding one small protected rabbit pelt; no huge hide. View southwest from the clean side. Shelter, hearth, river and other fixed features entirely OUT OF FRAME. Overcast daylight, tension through distance and watchfulness, no weapons upgrade, metal, modern objects, tattoos, duplicated body parts or labels.
images.review: Accepted: upright traveller and normal canid separated by open ground; spear held low with a tapered wooden point, no cast/strike/injury; grass garment removed, fox strip retained, small dirty frame and pelt, no changed hearth/shelter geography.
